title: K-flat module model of affine derived pullback
statement: Let f:X→Y be a morphism of affine schemes [def-pc-scheme], A=Γ(Y,O_Y), B=Γ(X,O_X), and φ=f.appTop:A→B. Let E∈D_QCoh(O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category] and Lf* be [def-pc-derived-pullback]. There is a K-flat complex P of A-modules [def-pc-module-kflat-complex] such that E is isomorphic to the localization of termwise tilde(P), restricted along the canonical isomorphism Y→Spec(A). Moreover Lf*(E) is isomorphic to the exact derived restriction along X→Spec(B) of Q(tilde(extendScalars(φ)(P))). The spectrum localization universe may differ from the common ambient one. No boundedness or flatness of φ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08DW, proof of (1) by compatibility with open restriction and the affine computation (2); Tag 06Z0

proof.text: Obtain a module complex M representing E from exists_affine_module_complex_representative.

Use the source library ModuleCat.hasFunctorialFlatResolution and the reduced LeftResolution.resolutionFunctor to construct P and its augmentation s to M. LeftResolution.kFlat_resolutionFunctor_obj proves P K-flat and kFlatResolutionNatTrans gives QuasiIso s. Tilde preserves monomorphisms by injectivity of localization maps and preserves cokernels by its adjunction. Hence tilde followed by exact chart restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Q of its image of s is an isomorphism; compose its inverse with E ≅ Q(restrict tilde M) to get eP:E ≅ Q(restrict tilde P). These are already proved source-library and Mathlib declarations; no ringed-site resolution theorem is used.
Apply affine_kFlat_pullback_chart_comparison to f,P,hP. Map eP through derivedPullback f and compose it with the chart comparison. Supply P,hP,eP and the composite as the existential witness.
